verdicts.why: Plain verb for keeping something from harm; no attitude toward the thing saved.
The standard theological term for redemption; it names a religious act without expressing approval or contempt beyond that meaning.
Legal/formal sense of reserving a right; no judgement carried.
Describes a ringing or whistling sound (a kettle, a bullet); descriptive, not evaluative.
Says a matter needs tact; it is the plain, even polite, member of the set beside 'touchy' and 'ticklish' and takes no side on the matter itself.
In the fragile/frail sense it states breakability; unlike 'flimsy' it neither sneers nor admires.
Admiring: choosing 'delicate' over 'thin', 'faint' or 'small' praises the thing as finely and pleasingly made, as 'slender' does against 'skinny'.
The 'soft'/'easily hurt' sense (a baby's delicate skin) describes susceptibility; any tenderness is faint and not a warning a learner needs.
Applied to humour, satire or craft it is praise for refinement; 'delicate irony' approves where 'subtle irony' merely describes.
Technical sense for a sensitive instrument; states precision without attitude.
